body:
The router does depend on `Type` from core, but because it exposes a class with member of type `Type`, it must also re-export `Type` or TypeScript is unhappy.

@mprobst @alexeagle any ideas?

I think that is WAI in TypeScript, if you don't re-export, downstream clients cannot understand your type signatures. You could re-export or relax the field to be of type `any`.

is the field private by chance? Because if so, then it'd be a valid feature request for TS to support this use case (not being required to re-export private fields).

The field needs to be public.

I think this is something the documentation system is going to have to
change to handle.

On Thu, Aug 13, 2015, 18:30 Martin Probst notifications@github.com wrote:

> I think that is WAI in TypeScript, if you don't re-export, downstream
> clients cannot understand your type signatures. You could re-export or
> relax the field to be of type any.
> 
> is the field private by chance? Because if so, then it'd be a valid
> feature request for TS to support this use case (not being required to
> re-export private fields).
> 
> —
> Reply to this email directly or view it on GitHub
> https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/3632#issuecomment-130911680.

Does this result in an error for users who import both typings? @jeffbcross checked that it should work.
If it's just documented twice, how severe an issue is that?

This should be innocuous for the user. I think `type Type = Function`, or `type Type = new (...args) => any`, or something like that.

We could extend dgeni to filter out certain duplicates. I suspect we'll encounter the same problem with animations, http, etc. It might be reasonable to solve the general issue of duplicate exports. Or we could hard code a work around for now.

I think this will only really happen with shared utils like the façades. Could we check if the given class originates from `src/facade/*` and just not export those definitions?

Or we could possibly relax the type there to `any`, but that makes me kind of sad, and also makes the documentation worse for that class.
@naomiblack – I'm going to unassign myself since this is not actionable on my end.
Assigning to Misko to think about best fix.

After some research here is what needs to be done:
1. Don't export `Type` from `router.ts`
2. include `///<reference path="./angular2.d.ts"/>` in the `router.d.ts` file. This can be done by updating `/Users/misko/work/angular/docs/typescript-definition-package/index.js` to include `./angular2.d.ts`
3. Have dgeni reffer to `Type` as `ng.Type` rather then `Type`

I know how do do step 1 and 2, (see this #3704) no idea how to do step 3. Re-asigning to @btford , as I am hoping that he knows how to do 3, if not reasign to @petebacondarwin.
